title: Pub Quiz Voices
eyebrow: BadCode Shorts · Pub Quiz: Housing · voices round 1
heading: Cast the voices
intro: Four voices per role, each reading that role's real lines plain: no accent, age or acting in the prompt (your "uncanny valley" rule). The accent is the voice itself: Google library voices, plus five designed from one plain sentence (London, Essex, West Midlands) because the library has no London voice. These are normal speech; the huddle lines get whispered once the voices are picked. Pick one per role, or note "older", "less posh" and so on.

groups.title: The quizmaster (BadCode)
groups.line: How much did councils in England spend on temporary accommodation last year? Nearest wins. Thirty seconds. / Twenty seconds. / Pens down. / Two point nine billion pounds. One point eight billion of it on B&Bs and nightly lets.

opts.label: a: designed: east London, forties, low
b: designed: south London, fifties, deep and rough
opts.warn: Whisper heard "nearest" and "pens" oddly: check by ear

opts.label: d: library: Manchester, 45
opts.warn: Whisper heard "How much did" as "Our watch": check by ear

groups.title: The student
groups.line: A hundred million? That's loads. / Every night... Say fifty quid a night. I don't know how much things are, I only buy CBD ramen suppositories. Times three-sixty-five. Times a hundred thousand rooms? / That's billions. That can't be right. / So they rent the same rooms every year? Why don't they just own them?

opts.label: a: designed: south London, twenty, light
b: library: Bristol, 22
opts.warn: Whisper heard "quid" as "good": check by ear

groups.line: More. I've done three of them B&B jobs for the council this year. Every room, every night. / Fuck off, get your own answers. / Every year. And at the end nobody owns a single brick.

groups.title: The banker
groups.line: Paying by the night is the dearest way to buy anything. It's billions with a B. Keep up, you morons. / Bob. / Now he gets it. / So buy the bricks.
